description:
window.selectTextIn(selector, text) selects the first occurrence of text inside the first element matching selector, as a user's selection would; call it in an eval. "The comment button" is the element with data-testid "message-selection-comment-btn". To check the message input's value exactly, eval JSON.stringify(document.querySelector('[data-testid="message-input"]').value) and compare it with the JSON string given. Tapping Comment on a touch screen injects a blockquote into the composer. Perform the steps in order. 1. Navigate to /c/basil. 2. The first commentable message ('[data-testid="message"][data-commentable="true"]') should contain "water the basil before noon". 3. Eval window.selectTextIn('[data-testid="message"][data-commentable="true"]', 'water the basil'). 4. The comment button should become visible, and it must be inside the viewport (its bounding rect intersects the window's innerWidth x innerHeight). 5. Tap it with a real touch held across frames: a touch step "start" on the comment button; then an eval that waits two animation frames, new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(r))); then a touch step "end". 6. The message input's value should become exactly "> water the basil

" (JSON), the message input must be the focused element (document.activeElement), and the comment button should become hidden. 7. Eval window.selectTextIn('[data-testid="message"][data-commentable="true"]', 'before noon'); the comment button should become visible. 8. Tap it: touch "start" on the comment button immediately followed by touch "end". 9. The message input's value should become exactly "> water the basil

> before noon

" (JSON), and the comment button should become hidden.

steps.expression: (function(){ const el = document.querySelector('[data-testid="message-selection-comment-btn"]'); const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect(); return rect.width > 0 && rect.height > 0 && rect.left < window.innerWidth && rect.top < window.innerHeight && rect.right > 0 && rect.bottom > 0; })()
